system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent Juniper Ridge Health, Inc.; counterparty is Cobalt Cloud Services LLC.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.",
  "Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.",
  "Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.",
  "Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty."
]

Finding submitted.

**Result: missing — inserted new Section 10.3 at the preferred position.**

- **Investigation:** Section 10 (10.1–10.2) only ends access "after any agreed transition period" and addresses Deliverables/refunds; Section 15 covers processing limits but no return/export/deletion; Section 16.5 returns only Confidential Information and defers Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15 — Section 11 does not exist. No transition-assistance or data-return obligation exists anywhere, so even the fallback fails and the walk-away risk (no data return) is live.
- **Cure:** One inserted clause carrying exactly the six preferred elements — assistance on expiry or termination for up to six months at then-current rates, Customer Data returned in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion after that return (not merely after assistance). No survival tails, procedures, or other non-element boilerplate added, and no neighbouring text rewritten.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Rule and exact checklists:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.",
  "Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.",
  "Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.",
  "Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.",
  "Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.",
  "Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.",
  "Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination."
]

Claimed finding status: missing

Claimed target and element mapping:
{"level":"preferred","mappings":[{"element":"Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]},{"element":"Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.","status":"addressed_by_operation","operationIndexes":[1]}]}

Finding rationale:
Section 10 (Effect of Expiry or Termination) contains no exit obligations for us: 10.1 merely ends access "after any agreed transition period" (no committed assistance duration or rates), and 10.2 covers only Deliverables and refunds. Section 15 governs processing but imposes no return, export, or deletion duty, and 16.5's return/destroy obligation is limited to Confidential Information and expressly refers Customer Data out to Sections 11 and 15 (Section 11 does not exist in the Agreement). The Agreement therefore fails even the fallback (90 days' assistance; export within 30 days) and risks the walk-away outcome of no data return. We insert a single clause at the preferred position: six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion after that return.

Original cited paragraphs:
p0041: 10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
p0042: 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
p0063: 16.5 On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Customer Data: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.
Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.
Confidential Information: 16.1 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.

Rendered operative language:
10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide transition assistance for up to six months after that expiry or termination at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty days after that expiry or termination, return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format; and (c) after that return, delete Customer Data from its systems and certify the deletion in writing.
16.5 On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.

Margin comment:
[Playbook] Section 10 ends the Services without any exit help or data return, so we add a short clause: up to six months of transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion after that return. We can fall back to 90 days of assistance with export within 30 days.

Rule and exact checklists:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

That is walk-away territory under T4C (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term), so it fails the fallback, and 30 days' notice cannot rest on the fallback band of 60-90 days. Section 10.2 refunds only prepaid *recurring* Fees for the period after termination, which is neither an express pro-rata refund nor a refund of prepaid non-recurring Fees, so the refund element is carried in the new clause. Vendor has no convenience right, which is favourable to us; we state that expressly rather than leaving it to inference. New Section 9.4 sits between 9.3 and 9.5 so the conforming cross-reference in Section 2.1 resolves, and the no-reduction restriction in 2.1 is preserved.

**Finding submitted — deviation (MINCOMMIT).**

- **Offending clause:** § 2.1 (p0012) — USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay for three years, "without reduction or termination rights." This is squarely in walk-away territory and fails all three fallback elements (no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up).
- **Conflict noted:** § 12.3 (p0044) has Vendor acknowledge Customer made no minimum-volume commitment — directly inconsistent with § 2.1.
- **Cure (preferred level, single surgical replace):** § 2.1 now reads "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment." The second preferred element is already met verbatim by § 7.1 (payment of Fees stated in each Order Form, with usage-based unit pricing), so nothing further was added.
- **Swept for other exposure:** no volume caps or shortfall penalties elsewhere; the § 22.2/22.3 "shortfall" language runs against Vendor underpayments and benefits us.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall ...", capturing every exit route, including the partial subscription terminations contemplated by 10.1.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Limb (a): "at Customer's request, provide transition assistance for up to six months after that expiry or termination". The request condition is general (not tied only to anticipated expiry) and the period is anchored to the actual expiry/termination date.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Limb (a) ends "at Vendor's then-current rates".

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "within thirty days after that expiry or termination, return all Customer Data" — the 30-day clock runs from termination, not from a request.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (b): "return all Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format".

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Limb (c): "after that return, delete Customer Data from its systems and certify the deletion in writing" — deletion is expressly sequenced after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same opening words: "On expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason".

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Up to six months of assistance exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (b) requires return of all Customer Data within thirty days after expiry or termination.

reasons: All six preferred elements are met by a single inserted paragraph; the position is complete at the preferred level (and a fortiori at the fallback).

Minimality holds: the insertion is a concise new clause for a missing obligation, nothing in 10.1, 10.2 or 16.5 is deleted or paraphrased, and no extras (survival tail, at-own-expense, escrow, procedures, additional remedies) are bolted on.

Extending the trigger to "any Order Form" is not an extra requirement: 10.1 already contemplates termination of individual subscription Services, so the scoping keeps the assistance and return duties operative on partial exits rather than adding a new commercial term.

Intent is preserved: the refund and Deliverable mechanics in 10.2, the access wind-down in 10.1, and the confidentiality return/destroy regime in 16.5 (with its backup and legal-retention carve-outs) all survive without contradiction; the new clause supplies the Customer Data duties 16.5 expressly leaves to other sections.

Residual, pre-existing defect not created by this edit but worth a one-line note to the counterparty: 16.5 refers Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15" and there is no Section 11 in the Agreement. Consider asking that the cross-reference be repointed to the new transition clause so the retained sentence does not dangle.

elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 2.1 now reads in full: "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment." This replaces the prior three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay and is reinforced by retained Section 12.3 ("Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."). No other rendered clause imposes a volume cap or shortfall charge on Customer; Section 7.1 expressly bars unidentified "minimum-use" charges.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 7.1: "Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form... unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify." The defined term "Fees" is limited to amounts "payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services," so payment obligations run only to ordered Services or usage-based pricing. No edit needed.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: it presupposes a surviving purchase commitment. After the edit no commitment exists at all (Section 2.1 as rendered negates any minimum purchase or volume obligation), so the condition does not apply and the customer-protective outcome is strictly better than a 12-month-limited commitment.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Conditional on there being a commitment to reduce. The offending "without reduction or termination rights" language was deleted with the commitment itself, so there is nothing left to reduce; the fallback mechanic is unnecessary rather than omitted.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Conditional on a shortfall mechanic existing. No rendered clause imposes a shortfall or take-or-pay penalty on Customer (the Section 22.2/22.3 shortfall references concern Vendor underpayment audits), so no true-up substitution is required.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty. (independent check of retained formulas)
elements.evidence: No retained instalment, liquidated-damages, or contingent make-whole formula survives in the rendered text; Section 7.1 permits only Fees identified in an Order Form and prohibits unidentified minimum-use charges.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single-sentence replacement of Section 2.1 delivers the express no-minimum-purchase-or-volume statement, and the second preferred element was already met by unedited Section 7.1 read with the defined term "Fees" (amounts payable under an Order Form).

The edit is minimal: exactly one operative sentence was replaced, the drafter added no survival tail, no procedure, no damages language, and no requirement outside the MINCOMMIT checklist. Customer-favourable retained language (Section 7.1's bar on unidentified minimum-use charges; Section 12.3's no-minimum-volume acknowledgement) was preserved rather than restated, so there is no duplicated operative term.

Intent is preserved and an internal contradiction is cured: the deleted take-or-pay directly conflicted with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no minimum-volume commitment. Pricing, Order Form mechanics, term, and audit provisions are untouched, and the edit leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference in the cited text.

Fallback elements are recorded as vacuously met because each is conditional on a surviving commitment or shortfall mechanic; none survives. Verify separately that no Order Form, exhibit, or termination-for-convenience clause elsewhere cross-references the deleted "Section 2.1 commitment" (e.g., a fee-schedule discount premised on the USD 2,000,000 volume) — if such a reference exists it must be conformed, otherwise the edit would leave a dangling cross-reference.

No severity escalation is warranted; the original clause was walk-away territory (multi-year take-or-pay expressly "without reduction or termination rights"), and the proposed language resolves it at the preferred position, with the fallback correctly offered in the margin comment rather than drafted into the operative text.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: New Section 9.4: "Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — both the Agreement and Order Form levels are covered, and the conforming edit to Section 2.1 ("without reduction rights but subject to Section 9.4") removes the retained bar on termination rights that would otherwise contradict it.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires "thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor" — exactly the 30-day written-notice ceiling, with no additional condition or approval.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4: "Vendor shall refund, on a pro-rata basis, all prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination." This is an express pro-rata basis (not merely inferred from a post-termination period) and covers all prepaid Fees, curing the narrower "prepaid recurring Fees" language retained in Section 10.2.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Second sentence of Section 9.4: "Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term." No retained provision (9.1–9.3, 9.5, 27.3) grants Vendor any no-cause exit, so there is no internal inconsistency.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 sets thirty days' notice, which is outside (and better than) the 60–90 day fallback band; the fallback notice parameter is therefore not satisfied on its literal terms.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the redline imposes no early-termination fee, and no retained clause (2.1 take-or-pay as amended, 9.x, 10.2) creates a convenience-exit penalty, so there is no fee to cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Exceeded in Customer's favour: Section 9.4 denies Vendor any convenience right during a committed term and no other clause grants one, so Vendor cannot terminate for convenience mid-term at all.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor has no convenience termination right under the amended Section 9, so no Vendor notice period is engaged.

reasons: All four preferred elements are met in operative text: new Section 9.4 supplies the Customer convenience right over both the Agreement and Order Forms, a 30-day written-notice trigger, an express pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees for the post-termination period, and an express denial of any Vendor convenience right during a committed term. The position is complete at the preferred level.
Fallback is incomplete only because the 30-day notice sits outside the 60–90 day band; that is irrelevant given the preferred level is fully met.

Minimality holds. The insertion tracks the model language and correctly omits the surplus "in whole or in part" (no partial-termination structure is required by the selected checklist). The only edit outside the new clause is the Section 2.1 conforming change, which is necessary because the retained words "or termination rights" would flatly contradict the new right; the Customer-favourable "without reduction" restriction is preserved rather than deleted.

Intent is preserved: Section 9.4 is placed between 9.3 and 9.5 so numbering and the new Section 2.1 cross-reference both resolve; Sections 9.1–9.3, 9.5 and 10.2 survive without contradiction (9.4's broader all-Fees pro-rata refund supplements, and does not conflict with, the retained recurring-Fees refund in 10.2, which the drafter correctly left intact rather than rewriting).

Minor drafting note only (not a defect requiring repair): "committed term" is used descriptively and is not a capitalised defined term; if the counterparty pushes back, anchor it to the three-year term in Section 8.1 / the take-or-pay period in Section 2.1.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Findings:
[{"id":"f-ip-5155a55e","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","rationale":"Section 14.1 already secures our ownership of Customer Data and independently owned IP, limits Vendor to processing that material solely to provide, secure, support and improve the Services (service delivery, not independent exploitation), and 14.4 rules out unilateral joint ownership; 14.3 preserves Vendor Technology ownership and routes embedded Vendor Technology to the perpetual 13.2 licence. The failure is 14.2: Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for us while our only licence is revocable, non-transferable and expires with the Order Form term. That fails the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables) — we lose access to bespoke reports, configurations and integrations we paid for at term end. We take the fallback rather than preferred, leaving Vendor's ownership of Deliverables and its generic tools and know-how intact, and simply upgrade the licence sentence.","proposal":"Replace the revocable, term-limited Deliverable licence in 14.2 with a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables for Customer's business.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-967127db","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","rationale":"Section 21 satisfies our preferred position on all material terms and comfortably clears the fallback. The cap is expressly mutual (\"The cap is mutual\"), set at the greater of Fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000; \"Fees\" (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the basis is not illusory. Section 21.2 excludes indirect and consequential damages mutually (and helpfully confirms data restoration, replacement services, notices and incident response are direct damages). Section 21.3's Excluded Claims sit outside the cap and cover confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's IP. Section 21.4 preserves liability that cannot lawfully be limited and survives failure of an exclusive remedy. No competing or one-sided cap appears elsewhere (the only other \"liability\" references are Vendor's insurance covenants in §18.1). The one shortfall from preferred wording is that the payment carve-out in §21.3 is limited to \"undisputed Fees for conforming Services\" rather than all Customer amounts due; that narrowing operates in our favour (it keeps disputed and non-Fee amounts inside the cap rather than exposing us to uncapped payment claims), so we note it rather than redline it. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-f67decf2","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 sits at or above our preferred position and is favourable to us. 24.1 lets Customer assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets without Vendor's consent (notice only, and \"Affiliate\" is defined at 1.1 by >50% control). 24.2 bars Vendor from assigning, delegating material performance, or transferring by change of control without our prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, and bars assignment to a direct Customer competitor. 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control, so the walk-away trigger is absent. 24.3 does not undercut 24.1: it applies only \"For other assignments\" (i.e., those outside the 24.1/24.2 carve-outs) and imposes a mutual not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard; 13.3 reinforces our ability to transfer licence rights on a permitted assignment. The only wording short of the ideal preferred formulation is that the competitor bar is limited to a \"direct\" competitor and is expressed as subject to our own consent — a minor sub-element noted here rather than redlined, since Vendor assignment already requires our consent in all cases. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-7d9be747","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 7.1 Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form. Fees are fixed during the initial term unless an Order Form expressly provides a usage-based unit price. Vendor may not impose a platform, support, administration, minimum-use, or similar charge that the Order Form does not identify.","rationale":"Searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalty\", \"early termination fee\", minimum/shortfall charges and acceleration return no Customer-payable liquidated or penal amount anywhere. Section 7.1 limits Customer's payment obligation to Fees stated in the Order Form and expressly bars Vendor from imposing unidentified minimum-use or similar charges; Section 27.3 lets Customer terminate \"without penalty\"; termination Sections 9.1-9.5 and 10.1-10.2 impose no exit fee and run refunds in Customer's favour. Section 22.2's undisputed audit shortfall and Section 21 liability caps are compensatory, not liquidated damages. The take-or-pay commitment in Section 2.1 is a minimum-volume obligation reviewed under MINCOMMIT and is not flagged twice here. The Agreement therefore sits at the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-a531b010","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","rationale":"The licence package sits at our preferred position. §13.1 grants the subscription right to \"Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf\" (affiliates and contractors covered, with no written-notice condition needed). §13.2 grants Customer and its Affiliates a \"perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence\" for paid-up software and Vendor Technology, satisfying the perpetual and irrevocable elements. §13.3 limits revocation or suspension to a \"material uncured payment or use breach affecting the licensed item, after notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure,\" meeting the subscription-termination element, and permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor; that cross-reference holds because §24.1 lets Customer assign without Vendor's consent to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets. The defined \"Affiliate\" (§1.1) is control-based and adequate. The only friction is §14.2, which describes the Deliverable licence as \"revocable, non-transferable\" and conflicts with §§13.2–13.3; consistent with the playbook we address revocability of Deliverable/IP rights once under the IP rule rather than flagging the same commercial term twice here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-aa0c1dbb","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.","rationale":"Section 7.2 imposes a most-favoured-nation obligation on us in Vendor's favour: before engaging another provider we must disclose and match any more favourable commercial offer we receive. This is the wrong direction and sits in walk-away territory — it is open-ended as to product, has no time limit, and contains no like-for-like comparison carve-outs, so it fails the fallback on every element. It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no most-favoured-customer commitment. We therefore take the preferred position and remove the Customer-side obligation; a Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would remain welcome.","proposal":"Remove the Customer-side disclose-and-match MFN obligation in Section 7.2.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-00a4a55e","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.","rationale":"Section 12.4 (second instance, p0046) binds Customer with an undefined-scope non-compete (\"any product or service that competes with Vendor\"), in any territory, for the term plus 24 months. That is walk-away territory on both counts (post-term restriction longer than 12 months and undefined competing scope) and fails every fallback element: no named product, post-term application, 24 months, and no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, which records that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. We therefore take the preferred position and convert the prohibition into an express permission, which removes the restriction and aligns 12.4 with 12.3. The separate no-hire restriction in the first Section 12.4 (p0045) is addressed under the no-hire rule, not here.","proposal":"Convert Section 12.4's term-plus-24-month non-compete into an express permission","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-b5a8fdcb","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.","rationale":"Section 12.4 is the only non-solicitation provision in the Agreement and it is walk-away territory: it binds Customer only (not mutual), covers every Vendor employee rather than personnel directly involved in the Services, runs 24 months past the term, expressly includes hiring and employing (a no-hire), and has no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches (\"regardless of how the employee applies\"). It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made \"no ... no-hire commitment\". We therefore take the preferred position and remove the restriction with a single minimal edit to the prohibitory operator and duration; no other paragraph cross-references Section 12.4, so no collateral changes are needed. Fallback (mutual, Services-involved personnel, 12 months, general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs, no no-hire) remains available if Vendor needs a covenant.","proposal":"Remove the one-way 24-month non-solicit/no-hire binding Customer","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-7a9ef531","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"Section 9 gives only cause-based, insolvency and Customer cause-like triggers (9.1-9.3), and Section 27.3 a force-majeure exit; there is no Customer termination-for-convenience right anywhere, and Section 2.1 expressly denies termination rights across a three-year committed term (Section 8.1). That is walk-away territory under T4C (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term), so it fails the fallback, and 30 days' notice cannot rest on the fallback band of 60-90 days. Section 10.2 refunds only prepaid *recurring* Fees for the period after termination, which is neither an express pro-rata refund nor a refund of prepaid non-recurring Fees, so the refund element is carried in the new clause. Vendor has no convenience right, which is favourable to us; we state that expressly rather than leaving it to inference. New Section 9.4 sits between 9.3 and 9.5 so the conforming cross-reference in Section 2.1 resolves, and the no-reduction restriction in 2.1 is preserved.","proposal":"Add Customer 30-day convenience termination with pro-rata refund of all prepaid Fees, bar Vendor convenience termination, and conform take-or-pay clause","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-audit-fd697e2e","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","rationale":"Section 22 meets the preferred position in full: audits are limited to once in any twelve-month period (22.1), require at least thirty days' prior written notice (22.1), occur during normal business hours (22.1), are conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality (22.1), Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent (22.2), and Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly (22.2). Section 23 (Records and Customer Assurance) contains no operative audit right binding Customer, and no other inspection or verification right against Customer appears in the document. No redline required.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-4a18e833","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.","rationale":"Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and is Vendor-favourable walk-away territory; it also directly conflicts with Section 28.2, which already grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County with only a customary temporary injunctive relief carve-out (that carve-out does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum). The shortest complete cure is to change the governing law in 28.1 to New York and delete the conflicting Singapore forum, leaving 28.2 as the sole venue; the preferred forum element is therefore already met verbatim.","proposal":"Replace Singapore governing law and Singapore exclusive jurisdiction with New York law, leaving 28.2's New York County forum as the sole venue.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-70be8bbe","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.","rationale":"Section 2.1 imposes a multi-year (three-year) USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly \"without reduction or termination rights\" — walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT, and it fails every fallback element (no 12-month limit, no 30-day reduction right, no true-up). It also contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment. We therefore target the preferred position with the shortest edit: replace the offending commitment sentence with an express no-minimum-purchase-or-volume statement. The second preferred element is already met by Section 7.1, which obliges Customer to pay only the Fees stated in each Order Form (with usage-based unit pricing where an Order Form so provides), so no further language is added. No other clause imposes volume caps or shortfall penalties on Customer (the Section 22.2/22.3 \"shortfall\" references concern Vendor underpayment audits).","proposal":"Replace the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay in Section 2.1 with an express no-minimum-commitment statement.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-33e30b33","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.","rationale":"Renewal terms sit at the playbook preferred position. Section 8.2 provides automatic renewal in successive twelve-month periods (no multi-year renewal), a Customer opt-out on only thirty days' written notice (well inside the 30-day preferred window), and a Vendor reminder at least sixty days before renewal, with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed. Section 8.3 caps renewal increases to recurring Fees at the lesser of CPI over the preceding twelve months and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods.
